classification.class: invalid read from truncated learn-spec width
classification.classification_note: ARVO metadata labels this sample `CWE-457`, but the exact staged OVS source plus the fixing diff ground a numeric truncation in `ofpact_learn_spec.n_bits` that misaligns learn-spec iteration and causes the invalid read.

bug_description.normalized: The staged 164-byte `ofctl_parse_target` witness has selector byte `0xDF` followed by the exact NUL-terminated string whose `learn(` argument begins with the staged long `tun_metadata7=` immediate literal and continues with `tun_metadata7=0`. Because the harness reads `data` through `const char *`, that selector is interpreted as a signed `char` on the crashing Linux build and the command expression reaches `OFPFC_ADD`, matching the saved `parse_ofp_str__ -> ofpacts_check` stack. `ofp_extract_actions()` therefore passes the entire suffix after `action=` into `ofpacts_parse_instructions()`, and because the `learn(` argument has no closing `)`, `learn_parse__()` keeps the whole suffix inside one learn invocation while `ofputil_parse_key_value()` treats `` as whitespace. The witness thus contains a first real learn token carrying that staged long `tun_metadata7` immediate value and a later real `tun_metadata7=0` token inside the same unterminated `learn(` string. Parsing the first full-field `tun_metadata7` token records a destination width in `unsigned int`, but the vulnerable `struct ofpact_learn_spec` stores `n_bits` as `uint8_t`, so `spec->n_bits = dst.n_bits` truncates that width while the parser still appends the full immediate payload for the first token. During `learn_check()`, `ofpact_learn_spec_next()` uses the truncated `spec->n_bits` to step partway through that first payload, landing inside it before the later real `tun_metadata7=0` header, and `OFPACT_LEARN_SPEC_FOR_EACH` reinterprets those payload bytes as a forged spec. `learn_check()` passes the forged `spec->src` into `mf_check_src()`, and `mf_check__()` dereferences its bogus `sf->field` pointer at `lib/meta-flow.c:2511`, matching the staged MemorySanitizer `SEGV` on READ. The fix widens `ofpact_learn_spec.n_bits` to `uint32_t` so the iterator uses the full stored width.

source.description: This is the first project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled action substring returned after `action=` and materializes the vulnerable `ofpact_learn` state.
source.value_from: Bytes 1..162 plus the terminating NUL at byte 163 of the staged 164-byte `poc`: the exact string begins `action=learn(`, contains the staged long `tun_metadata7=` immediate literal, then one carriage return (`0x0d`), then a later real `tun_metadata7=0` token, and reaches NUL without any closing `)`. `ofp_extract_actions()` passes that whole suffix after `action=` into the action parser, so the `` stays inside the `learn(` argument instead of becoming trailing match text. Byte 0 is the harness selector.

sink.description: The forged interior spec created from the first immediate payload passes a bogus `struct mf_subfield` into `mf_check__`. Evaluating `sf->field->n_bits` dereferences its non-null invalid `field` pointer and triggers the observed MemorySanitizer SEGV on READ.

root_cause.description: This assignment stores the wide destination width into `spec->n_bits`, whose vulnerable type is `uint8_t` in `include/openvswitch/ofp-actions.h`. The narrowing truncates the length later used to step across immediate data. The fix widens `n_bits` to `uint32_t`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Parsing the attacker-chosen full-field destination `tun_metadata7` materializes the wide bit width that later overflows the vulnerable `uint8_t spec->n_bits` storage.

parser_admitted.description: The staged crash stack reaches `parse_ofp_str__` line 1737, which is only executed after `ofpacts_parse_instructions(act_str, &pp)` succeeds and materializes the parsed action list.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness reads selector byte `0xDF` through `const char *`, so on the crashing Linux build the command expression yields `OFPFC_ADD`; it then forwards the tail string into `ofctl_parse_flow`, keeping `parse_ofp_flow_mod_str()` on its `F_ACTIONS` path.

`ofp_extract_actions()` null-terminates the original flow string at `action` and hands the whole unterminated `learn(` suffix, containing the staged long `tun_metadata7=` immediate literal followed by `tun_metadata7=0`, to the action parser, so the later `tun_metadata7=0` token stays inside the same `learn(` argument.

Inside `learn_parse__()`, `` is tokenized as whitespace, so the witness yields a first oversized immediate `tun_metadata7=` token carrying the staged long value and a later real `tun_metadata7=0` token; parsing the first full-field token stores its width in `spec->n_bits` as `uint8_t` while still appending the first token's full immediate payload.

When the parsed learn action is validated, `ofpact_learn_spec_next()` uses the truncated width to step into the first token's immediate payload before the later real `tun_metadata7=0` header, and `learn_check()` treats the interior bytes as a forged spec.
The bogus second spec contributes a fake `struct mf_subfield`, and `mf_check__()` dereferences its invalid `field` pointer at line 2511, matching the observed MemorySanitizer invalid read.

fine_trace.note: The staged selector byte `0xDF` is read through `const char *stream`; on the crashing Linux build that makes `stream[0]` a negative `char`, so this expression yields `0` (`OFPFC_ADD`). `parse_ofp_flow_mod_str()` therefore takes one of the cases whose `fields` mask includes `F_ACTIONS`, matching the saved `parse_ofp_str__ -> ofpacts_check` stack.

Because step 1 made `fields & F_ACTIONS` true, earlier `ofp_extract_actions()` overwrote the initial `action` with `\0` and returned the entire suffix after `=`. This call therefore consumes the exact attacker-controlled action string whose `learn(` argument contains the staged long `tun_metadata7=` immediate literal followed by `\rtun_metadata7=0`, with no closing `)` and no trailing match text outside the action parser, to build the in-memory `ofpact_learn` action.

Because step 2 supplied an unterminated `learn(` argument, `ofputil_parse_key_value()` keeps scanning until the final NUL; its delimiter set treats `\r` as whitespace, so the loop first yields `name="tun_metadata7"` with the staged long immediate value and later yields a real second token `name="tun_metadata7", value="0"` from the same `learn(` string.

When `learn_parse_spec()` handles the first token from step 3, parsing destination name `tun_metadata7` with no `[]` slice materializes the full-field width into `sf->n_bits`. On the crashing path that accepted full-field width exceeds what the vulnerable `uint8_t spec->n_bits` can represent.

The wide destination width from step 4 is stored into `spec->n_bits`, but that field is declared as `uint8_t` in the vulnerable `struct ofpact_learn_spec`. The executed store keeps only the low 8 bits, truncating the length that later drives learn-spec iteration.

The same first-token immediate branch still appends payload bytes using the original wide `dst.n_bits`, so the serialized learn action contains the full immediate payload after the first spec header even though step 5 truncated the stored `spec->n_bits`. Any later real spec from step 3, including `tun_metadata7=0`, is serialized only after this full payload region.

When `learn_check()` iterates learn specs, the skip length is computed from truncated `spec->n_bits`. Because step 6 laid out more immediate bytes than this reduced skip covers, the returned pointer lands inside the first token's immediate payload before any later serialized header, including the witness's later real `tun_metadata7=0` spec from step 3.

The misadvanced pointer from step 7 is still before `ofpact_learn_spec_end(learn)`, so `OFPACT_LEARN_SPEC_FOR_EACH` enters a bogus interior iteration on first-payload bytes. On the crashing execution those bytes decode to a forged spec with `src_type == NX_LEARN_SRC_FIELD`, and line 52 passes the forged `spec->src` subfield to `mf_check_src()`.

The forged subfield from step 8 has a non-null invalid `sf->field` pointer and nonzero `sf->n_bits`, so the third branch in `mf_check__()` dereferences `sf->field->n_bits`. MemorySanitizer reports the resulting invalid READ/SEGV exactly at this line.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The fixing commit widens `struct ofpact_learn_spec.n_bits` from `uint8_t` to `uint32_t`, removing the truncation that makes `ofpact_learn_spec_next()` walk into the appended immediate payload.

poc.trigger: The staged 164-byte `ofctl_parse_target` witness uses selector byte `0xDF` and the exact tail string from `poc`, whose `learn(` argument contains the staged long `tun_metadata7=` immediate literal, one ``, and then `tun_metadata7=0` before the required NUL terminator. On the observed Linux build the selector drives the `F_ACTIONS` path; `ofp_extract_actions()` passes the whole unterminated `learn(` suffix into `learn_parse__()`, which tokenizes the single `` as whitespace. The first real `tun_metadata7=` token carrying that long immediate value creates an immediate full-field learn spec whose width overflows `uint8_t spec->n_bits`, and `learn_check()` later iterates into that first token's appended immediate payload before the later real `tun_metadata7=0` token's header and crashes in `mf_check__` on the forged interior spec.

format.name: 164-byte `ofctl_parse_target` learn-action witness buffer
format.contract: Exactly the staged 164-byte input in `gt_results/arvo_11869/poc`: byte 0 is selector `0xDF`; bytes 1..162 are the precise NUL-free flow string already staged in that file, beginning with `action=learn(`, then the exact immediate token `tun_metadata7=0xCCCCCCCCCCCCCCeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC80`, then one `0x0d` carriage return, then `tun_metadata7=0`; byte 163 is the required NUL terminator. The string contains no closing `)` before the NUL. `ofp_extract_actions()` therefore passes the whole suffix after `action=` into `learn_parse__()`, and the single `0x0d` is tokenized as whitespace, producing a first oversized immediate `tun_metadata7=` token carrying that exact value and a later real `tun_metadata7=0` token inside one unterminated `learn(`. This exact first token is the load-bearing trigger: its full-field width exceeds the vulnerable `uint8_t spec->n_bits` storage, and `learn_check()` later reinterprets bytes from that first token's appended immediate payload as a forged spec before it ever reaches the later real token's header.
